items.rationale: Covered under 5.2.6(b) as costs of inspecting and assessing the damage to determine cause and extent, up to the EUR 3,000 per event limit. Reference Case 20 shows t >= 481 for a similar assessment call.

Covered under 5.2.6(a) as costs of locating the point(s) of water escape, up to EUR 1,000 per event. Reference Case 20 shows t >= 707 for a similar leak detection, but this is likely a single flat-rate charge, so t = 707.

Technician time for leak detection is covered under 5.2.6(a) as part of the locating-the-leak cost, but if already included in the flat-rate leak detection (item 2), only the measured-quantity charge is indemnified (7.1.8(c)). Reference Case 20: technician time is included in the flat rate, so this is not separately indemnified.
One vehicle charge per contractor per invoice is covered under 5.2.6(c), up to EUR 70 net plus VAT. Reference Case 20: t >= 76 for vehicle costs for leak detection.

items.description: Repair of the copper joints verified as actively leaking (seal/renew failed sections)
items.rationale: Repair of only the leaking sections is covered under 2.4.3 and 7.1.5, as only those parts were affected. Reference Case 20: similar repair t between 157 and 220. Use midpoint.

items.description: Precautionary replacement of the remaining original copper supply run across the ground floor (sections not themselves shown to be leaking)
items.rationale: Work on sections not themselves shown to be leaking is excluded under 2.4.3 and 7.1.5; only affected parts are covered. Reference Case 20 and policy: t = 0.

items.description: Upgrade surcharge – premium multilayer composite piping in lieu of standard copper
items.rationale: No betterment over pre-loss standard is indemnified (7.1.9); only like-for-like is covered. Upgrade surcharge is excluded. Reference Case 20 and policy: t = 0.
One vehicle charge per contractor per invoice is covered under 5.2.6(c), up to EUR 70 net plus VAT. Reference Case 20: t >= 76 for vehicle costs for plumbing.
